items.q: 윗글 1번 문장과 같이 「There + 동사 + 주어」 어순을 쓴 문장 중 어법상 옳은 것은?
choices: There stands two old trees in front of the school.
There stood two old trees in front of the school.
There stood two old tree in front of the school.
There were stood two old trees in front of the school.
There two stood old trees in front of the school.
items.exp: 「There + 동사 + 주어」에서 동사는 뒤에 오는 주어의 수에 맞춰요. two old trees는 복수 주어이고 과거 시제이므로 stood가 맞아요. stands는 단수 동사라 주어와 맞지 않고, two old tree는 복수 표현이 틀려요.
items.passage: Years ago, there lived a boy in a small village in Scotland.

items.q:
[요약] 윗글을 읽고 아래 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Angus made socks for the cold sparrows. Later, the sparrows (A) ___ their socks to Angus's store to help him, and the store became (B) ___ with people.
choices: (A) returned - (B) crowded
(A) sold - (B) empty
(A) kept - (B) crowded
(A) returned - (B) empty
(A) hid - (B) quiet
items.exp: 참새들은 Angus가 곤경에 처하자 양말을 가게로 돌려주었고(flew into the sock store and piled their socks), 그 결과 가게는 손님들로 붐볐어요(was crowded with customers). kept나 hid는 돌려준 내용과 맞지 않고, empty와 quiet는 가게가 붐볐다는 내용과 반대예요.
items.passage:
Angus made more and more socks because he knew other sparrows were shaking in the cold weather, too.
But he didn't realize that he used up all the wool in the machine.
Angus honestly said, "Sorry, I made socks for sparrows. They were shaking in the cold weather."
After a while, Bruce brought the other sparrows together and said, "We need to return the socks."
Bruce added, "Angus is in trouble because of our socks. We should help him."
The sparrows flew into the sock store and piled their socks on the table.
The store was crowded with customers.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [that]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: I heard that the store was closed yesterday.
That cat is Bruce's friend.
Is that your sock machine?
The boy that lives next door is my classmate.
She was so tired that she went to bed early.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 that은 선행사 a small store를 꾸미며 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사예요. The boy that lives ~의 that만 선행사 The boy를 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사이고, 나머지는 접속사, 지시형용사, 지시대명사예요.
items.passage: Angus's father owned a small store [that] made socks, and Angus sometimes helped him.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [it]과 [them]이 가리키는 것을 순서대로 짝지은 것은?
choices: the store - socks
the department store - customers
the store - customers
Angus's father - customers
the sock machine - villagers
items.exp: it은 앞에 나온 The store를, them은 many customers를 가리켜요. 가게가 손님을 많이 잃었다는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Angus's father owned a small store that made socks, and Angus sometimes helped him. The store used to have many customers, but recently [it] lost a lot of [them].

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [used to]와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: Wood is used to make paper.
My uncle used to be a teacher, but now he is a farmer.
I am used to getting up early.
She used the machine to make socks.
We use this room to study.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 used to는 '(과거에) ~였다/~하곤 했다'를 뜻하는 「used to + 동사원형」이에요. My uncle used to be ~가 같은 쓰임이에요. Wood is used to make ~는 수동태 + 목적의 to부정사, I am used to -ing는 '~에 익숙하다'라서 달라요.
items.passage: The store [used to] have many customers, but recently it lost a lot of them.

items.q: 다음 중 「used to」의 쓰임이 어법상 옳은 문장은?
choices: He used to going to school by bus.
They used to played soccer after school.
My grandfather is used to walk in the park every morning.
There used to be a bakery near my school.
She uses to live in Busan.
items.exp: 「used to + 동사원형」이므로 There used to be ~가 맞아요. going과 played는 동사원형이 아니고, be used to 뒤에는 동명사가 와서 walk는 틀리며, uses to는 존재하지 않는 형태예요.
items.passage: Angus's father owned a small store that made socks, and Angus sometimes helped him. The store used to have many customers, but recently it lost a lot of them.

items.q: 윗글 7번 문장의 start처럼 목적어로 to부정사와 동명사를 모두 쓸 수 있는 동사가 쓰인 문장 중 어법상 옳은 것은?
choices: She enjoys to read comic books.
He decided going to the store.
The children started singing in the garden.
I want making a hat for my mom.
They finished to clean the room.
items.exp: start는 to부정사와 동명사를 모두 목적어로 취해서 started singing(= started to sing)이 맞아요. enjoy와 finish는 동명사만, decide와 want는 to부정사만 목적어로 취하므로 나머지는 틀려요.
items.passage: Villagers started buying socks from a big department store.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 어색한 문장은?
choices: The mountain was covered with fog this morning.
The playground is crowded with students after school.
The glass was filled with orange juice.
The museum is located in the center of the city.
My brother was surprised on the loud noise.
items.exp: 수동태에서 be surprised는 at(또는 by)과 함께 쓰므로 surprised on은 틀려요. 나머지는 be covered with, be crowded with, be filled with, be located in으로 모두 바른 표현이에요.
items.passage: The tree [was covered with] snow.

items.q: 윗글 10번 문장의 saw Bruce raising his feet처럼 지각동사 뒤에 목적격 보어가 오는 문장 중 어법상 옳은 것은?
choices: I heard the baby cried in the next room.
I heard the baby crying in the next room.
I heard the baby to cry in the next room.
I heard the baby cries in the next room.
I heard the baby was cry in the next room.
items.exp: 지각동사(see, hear 등)의 목적격 보어로는 동사원형 또는 현재분사(-ing)를 써요. heard the baby crying이 맞고, 과거형 cried, to cry, 3인칭 단수형 cries는 모두 쓸 수 없어요.
items.passage: Angus saw Bruce [raising] his feet one by one.

items.q: Angus가 "Your feet are cold!"라고 말한 근거로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: Bruce가 눈 덮인 나무 위에서 발을 하나씩 들어 올리는 모습을 보았기 때문에
Bruce가 Angus의 주머니 속에서 계속 떨고 있었기 때문에
다른 참새들이 Angus에게 양말을 만들어 달라고 부탁했기 때문에
Bruce가 Angus에게 직접 발이 시리다고 말했기 때문에
아버지가 겨울에는 참새들의 발이 차갑다고 알려 주었기 때문에
items.exp: Angus는 Bruce가 눈 덮인 나무에서 발을 하나씩 드는 것을 보고 발이 차갑다고 짐작했어요. 나머지는 윗글에 나오지 않는 내용이에요.
items.passage:
One cold winter morning, Bruce and the other sparrows were in a tree.
The tree was covered with snow.
Angus saw Bruce raising his feet one by one.
"Your feet are cold! Maybe I can help you," said Angus.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 (a) close와 (b) closed에 대한 설명으로 옳은 것은?
choices: (a) 동사 '닫다', 발음 [klouz] / (b) 형용사 '친한', 발음 [klous]
(a) 형용사 '친한', 발음 [klous] / (b) 동사 '닫다', 발음 [klouz]
(a) 형용사 '친한', 발음 [klouz] / (b) 동사 '닫다', 발음 [klous]
(a) 부사 '가깝게', 발음 [klous] / (b) 동사 '닫다', 발음 [klouz]
(a), (b) 모두 동사 '닫다', 발음 [klouz]
items.exp: (a)는 '친한'이라는 뜻의 형용사로 [klous]로 발음하고, (b)는 '(문을) 닫다'라는 뜻의 동사로 [klouz]로 발음해요. (a)는 friend를 꾸미는 형용사라 부사가 아니에요.
items.passage:
A sparrow, Bruce, was his [close] friend.
After the store [closed] for the night, Angus sat in front of the sock machine.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [with]와 의미가 같은 것은?
choices: I want a house with a big garden.
I went to the park with my dog.
She cut the paper with scissors.
Come with me to the store.
He talked with his teacher.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 with는 '~이 있는, ~을 가진'이라는 소유의 뜻이에요. a house with a big garden의 with가 같아요. 나머지는 '~와 함께'나 '~로(도구)'의 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Warm and soft winter socks [with] red stripes!

items.q:
윗글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 알맞은 곳은?
"Son, something strange happened. Someone took all of our wool."
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
items.exp: 주어진 문장은 아버지가 Angus에게 한 말이에요. 22번 문장의 called Angus 뒤에 와야 하고, 이 말에 대한 반응으로 Angus가 Sorry, I made socks for sparrows.라고 대답하므로 22번과 24번 사이인 ②가 알맞아요.
items.passage: But they couldn't find the same socks anywhere. ( ① ) At the same time in the sock store, Angus's father called Angus. ( ② ) Angus honestly said, "Sorry, I made socks for sparrows. They were shaking in the cold weather." ( ③ ) Bruce was listening silently in Angus's pocket. ( ④ ) After a while, Bruce brought the other sparrows together and said, "We need to return the socks." ( ⑤ )

items.q: 윗글의 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
choices: (A) because of - (B) because
(A) because - (B) because
(A) because of - (B) because of
(A) because - (B) because of
(A) so - (B) because of
items.exp: (A) 뒤에는 he knew ~라는 「주어 + 동사」가 오므로 접속사 because가, (B) 뒤에는 our socks라는 명사구가 오므로 전치사구 because of가 알맞아요.
items.passage:
Angus made more and more socks ( A ) he knew other sparrows were shaking in the cold weather, too.
Bruce added, "Angus is in trouble ( B ) our socks. We should help him."

items.q: 윗글 15번 문장의 [too]가 의미하는 바로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: Angus도 추워서 떨고 있었다.
양말 가게도 손님이 줄어 어려웠다.
Bruce뿐 아니라 다른 참새들도 추위에 떨고 있었다.
다른 참새들도 붉은 줄무늬 양말을 좋아했다.
기계 속의 양모도 많이 줄어들었다.
items.exp: too는 '~도'라는 뜻으로, 추위에 발을 들던 Bruce 말고도 다른 참새들이 추운 날씨에 떨고 있었다는 뜻이에요.
items.passage:
One cold winter morning, Bruce and the other sparrows were in a tree.
Angus saw Bruce raising his feet one by one.
Angus made more and more socks because he knew other sparrows were shaking in the cold weather, [too].

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [that]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: The girl that is singing on the stage is my cousin.
That hat looks great on you.
Is that your bag?
This is the book that I borrowed yesterday.
I think that the movie was exciting.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 that은 realize의 목적어가 되는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사예요. I think that ~의 that이 같아요. 나머지는 각각 주격 관계대명사, 지시형용사, 지시대명사, 목적격 관계대명사예요.
items.passage: But he didn't realize [that] he used up all the wool in the machine.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Angus는 기계의 양모를 모두 써 버린 줄 몰랐다.
Angus는 양모가 부족하다는 것을 알면서도 양말을 만들었다.
Angus는 Bruce 한 마리만을 위해 양말을 만들었다.
다른 참새들은 추위를 피해 먼 곳으로 떠났다.
Angus의 아버지가 양모를 더 사다 주었다.
items.exp: But he didn't realize that he used up all the wool로 보아 양모를 다 쓴 사실을 몰랐어요. other sparrows가 떨고 있어서 더 많이 만들었으므로 Bruce만을 위한 것도 아니에요.
items.passage:
Angus made more and more socks because he knew other sparrows were shaking in the cold weather, too.
But he didn't realize that he used up all the wool in the machine.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [something warm]처럼 「-thing + 형용사」 어순이 어법상 옳은 문장은?
choices: Is there anything special in the box?
Is there special anything in the box?
I need new something for the party.
She told me strange something about him.
Do you want sweet something to eat?
items.exp: -thing으로 끝나는 대명사는 형용사가 뒤에서 꾸며요. anything special이 맞고 나머지는 형용사가 앞에 와서 틀려요.
items.passage: The next day, the sparrows were wearing [something warm].

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 쓰임이 나머지와 다른 것은?
items.exp: ⓐ~ⓓ는 「was/were + -ing」의 과거진행형이고, ⓔ는 「are + -ing」의 현재진행형이에요. 36번 문장은 Now가 있어서 지금 진행 중인 동작을 나타내요.
items.passage:
The next day, the sparrows ⓐ[were wearing] something warm.
They ⓑ[were wearing] cute socks with red stripes!
Angus honestly said, "Sorry, I made socks for sparrows. They ⓒ[were shaking] in the cold weather."
Bruce ⓓ[was listening] silently in Angus's pocket.
Now the villagers ⓔ[are all wearing] warm socks with red stripes.

items.q: 윗글 19번 문장의 as soon as를 참고하여 "그녀는 집에 도착하자마자 샤워를 했다."를 영어로 옮긴 문장으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: As soon as she arrives home, she took a shower.
As soon she arrived home, she took a shower.
As soon as arrived she home, she took a shower.
As soon as she arrived home, she took a shower.
As soon as she arrived home, she takes a shower.
items.exp: as soon as는 '~하자마자'이며 「as soon as + 주어 + 동사」 어순이에요. 과거의 일이므로 두 동사 모두 과거형(arrived, took)이어야 해요.
items.passage: [As soon as] people saw the socks, they hurried to the department store.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 가리키는 대상이 나머지와 다른 것은?
items.exp: ⓐ people, ⓑ they, ⓒ We, ⓔ they는 모두 마을 사람들이고, ⓓ them은 앞의 the socks that the sparrows are wearing(참새들이 신은 양말)을 가리켜요.
items.passage: As soon as ⓐ[people] saw the socks, ⓑ[they] hurried to the department store. They asked, "ⓒ[We] want the socks that the sparrows are wearing. Where can we buy ⓓ[them]?" But ⓔ[they] couldn't find the same socks anywhere.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [that]을 생략할 수 있는 문장은?
choices: The girl that won the race is my sister.
The hat that my aunt gave me is too big.
I like that hat very much.
That is my cousin from Busan.
He is the man that lives next door.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 that은 목적격 관계대명사라서 생략할 수 있어요. The hat that my aunt gave me의 that도 gave의 목적어 역할이라 생략할 수 있어요. 주격 관계대명사 that, 지시형용사/지시대명사 that은 생략할 수 없어요.
items.passage: They asked, "We want the socks [that] the sparrows are wearing. Where can we buy them?"

items.q: 윗글 21번 문장과 의미가 같은 것은?
choices: They could find the same socks somewhere in the village.
They could find the same socks everywhere in the village.
They could find the same socks only at the department store.
They could find the same socks nowhere in the village.
They couldn't find some socks in the village.
items.exp: not ~ anywhere는 '어디에서도 ~않다'라는 뜻이라 nowhere를 쓴 문장과 의미가 같아요. somewhere, everywhere는 어딘가/어디에서나 찾았다는 반대 뜻이에요.
items.passage: But they couldn't find the same socks [anywhere].

items.q: 윗글에서 아버지가 말한 [something strange]가 가리키는 것은?
choices: 참새들이 붉은 줄무늬 양말을 신고 있는 일
가게의 양모가 모두 없어진 일
가게의 손님이 백화점으로 가 버린 일
양말 기계가 고장 나 버린 일
Angus가 아침부터 사라진 일
items.exp: 바로 뒤 문장 Someone took all of our wool.이 something strange의 내용이에요. 양모가 모두 사라진 일을 가리켜요.
items.passage:
At the same time in the sock store, Angus's father called Angus.
"Son, [something strange] happened. Someone took all of our wool."
Angus honestly said, "Sorry, I made socks for sparrows. They were shaking in the cold weather."

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [honestly]와 [silently]처럼 동사를 꾸미는 부사가 올바르게 쓰인 문장은?
choices: The boy walked quiet into the room.
She sings beautiful in the choir.
He answered the question easy.
The children played happy in the garden.
The boy walked quietly into the room.
items.exp: 동사를 꾸미는 말은 형용사가 아니라 부사여야 해요. quietly만 부사 형태로 바르게 쓰였고 나머지는 quiet, beautiful, easy, happy 같은 형용사를 썼어요.
items.passage:
Angus [honestly] said, "Sorry, I made socks for sparrows. They were shaking in the cold weather."
Bruce was listening [silently] in Angus's pocket.

items.q: 윗글 26번 문장에서 Bruce가 말한 [We]가 가리키는 것으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: Angus와 Bruce
마을 사람들
Bruce를 포함한 모든 참새들
Bruce를 제외한 다른 참새들
Angus의 아버지와 Angus
items.exp: Bruce가 다른 참새들을 모아 놓고 말한 것이므로 We는 말하는 Bruce 자신과 다른 참새들, 즉 모든 참새들이에요.
items.passage: After a while, Bruce brought the other sparrows together and said, "[We] need to return the socks."

items.q: 윗글 26번 문장의 We need to return the socks.와 의미가 가장 다른 것은?
choices: We have to return the socks.
We should return the socks.
We must return the socks.
We are supposed to return the socks.
We can return the socks.
items.exp: need to, have to, should, must, be supposed to는 모두 '~해야 한다'는 의무·필요를 나타내요. can은 능력이나 가능을 나타내서 의미가 달라요.
items.passage: After a while, Bruce brought the other sparrows together and said, "We [need to] return the socks."

items.q: 윗글 27번 문장 Do we have to?와 같은 형태로 쓴 문장 중 어법상 옳은 것은?
choices: Does she has to wake up early tomorrow?
Do she have to wake up early tomorrow?
Does she have to waking up early tomorrow?
Does she have to wake up early tomorrow?
She doesn't has to wake up early tomorrow.
items.exp: have to의 의문문은 「Do/Does + 주어 + have to + 동사원형」이에요. 주어가 she이면 Does를 쓰고, Does 뒤에는 동사원형 have가 와야 해요.
items.passage: "[Do we have to]? We like these socks," said the other sparrows.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
choices: We stayed home because of it snowed heavily.
We stayed home because the heavy snow.
We stayed home because of we were tired.
We stayed home because of the heavy snow.
We were late because the traffic jam.
items.exp: because of 뒤에는 명사(구)가 와요. the heavy snow가 맞고, 「주어 + 동사」가 오면 because를 써야 해요. 나머지는 because 뒤에 명사만 있거나 because of 뒤에 절이 와서 틀려요.
items.passage: Bruce added, "Angus is in trouble [because of] our socks. We should help him."

items.q: 윗글에서 Bruce가 말한 "Angus is in trouble"의 상황으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 가게의 양모를 허락 없이 모두 써서 곤란해진 상황
양말 때문에 백화점 주인에게 사과해야 하는 상황
참새들이 양말을 돌려주지 않아 가게가 문을 닫게 된 상황
양말에 붉은 줄무늬가 없어서 손님이 화를 내는 상황
Bruce가 주머니에서 나오지 않아 학교에 늦게 된 상황
items.exp: 아버지가 양모가 모두 없어졌다고 했고 Angus가 참새들에게 줄 양말을 만들었다고 털어놓은 장면이에요. 그래서 Angus가 곤경에 처했다고 한 것이에요.
items.passage:
At the same time in the sock store, Angus's father called Angus.
"Son, something strange happened. Someone took all of our wool."
Angus honestly said, "Sorry, I made socks for sparrows. They were shaking in the cold weather."
Bruce added, "[Angus is in trouble] because of our socks. We should help him."

items.q: 윗글의 흐름에 맞게 (A)~(C)를 배열한 것으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: Bruce의 제안(26번)에 다른 참새들이 Do we have to?라고 되묻고(B), Bruce가 Angus가 곤경에 처했다고 덧붙이며(A), 마지막에 참새들이 동의해요(C).
items.passage:
After a while, Bruce brought the other sparrows together and said, "We need to return the socks."
(A) Bruce added, "Angus is in trouble because of our socks. We should help him."
(B) "Do we have to? We like these socks," said the other sparrows.
(C) The sparrows agreed, "Alright then."

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [flew]와 [piled]처럼 접속사로 연결된 두 부분의 형태가 같은 문장은?
choices: The boy took off his hat and puts it on the chair.
The boy took off his hat and put it on the chair.
The boy took off his hat and putting it on the chair.
The boy took off his hat and to put it on the chair.
The boy took off his hat and he putting it on the chair.
items.exp: and로 연결된 두 동사는 같은 형태(병렬)여야 해요. took off와 put이 모두 과거형이에요. puts는 현재형, putting과 to put은 형태가 달라 병렬이 깨져요.
items.passage: The sparrows [flew] into the sock store and [piled] their socks on the table.

items.q: What is the main reason that people rushed into the sock store?
choices: Angus's father was giving away socks for free.
They found the socks they wanted on the table.
The department store was closed that day.
They wanted to see the sparrows' new hats.
Bruce called them to the store.
items.exp: 사람들은 참새들이 신은 양말을 사려 했지만 찾지 못하다가(21번), 참새들이 가게 탁자에 양말을 쌓아 놓자 "These are the socks that I want!"라며 몰려들었어요.
items.passage:
They asked, "We want the socks that the sparrows are wearing. Where can we buy them?"
But they couldn't find the same socks anywhere.
The sparrows flew into the sock store and piled their socks on the table.
Just then, people rushed into the store.
Someone said, "Finally! These are the socks that I want!"

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [has come back]과 같은 용법(결과)으로 쓰인 현재완료 문장은?
choices: I have lived in Seoul for ten years.
I have never seen a sparrow wearing socks.
Have you ever eaten kimchi?
He has just finished his homework.
She has lost her key, so she can't open the door.
items.exp: has come back은 과거의 일이 현재까지 영향을 남기는 결과 용법이에요. has lost her key(열쇠를 잃어버려서 지금 없다)가 같아요. 나머지는 계속, 경험, 경험, 완료 용법이에요.
items.passage: "Angus, your kind heart [has come back] to us as a great gift!" said his father.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [as]와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: She works as a nurse at a hospital.
As soon as I arrived, it started to rain.
He ran as fast as he could.
As it was cold, we stayed home.
She sings as well as her sister.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 as는 '~로(서)'라는 뜻의 전치사예요. works as a nurse의 as가 같아요. 나머지는 as soon as, as ~ as, 이유의 접속사 as, as well as예요.
items.passage: "Angus, your kind heart has come back to us [as] a great gift!" said his father.

items.q: 윗글 37번 문장 Oh, dogs and cats are, too!에서 생략된 말은?
choices: warm and soft
the villagers
wearing warm socks with red stripes
shaking in the cold weather
crowded with customers
items.exp: 앞 문장의 서술 부분 wearing warm socks with red stripes가 반복되어 생략되었어요. 개와 고양이도 따뜻한 양말을 신고 있다는 뜻이에요.
items.passage:
Now the villagers are all wearing warm socks with red stripes.
Oh, dogs and cats are, too!

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 테레사는 인도에서 병원을 지어 가난한 사람들을 도왔다.
왕가리 마타이는 인도에서 나무를 심는 일을 했다.
장기려는 케냐에서 사람들의 권리를 위해 싸웠다.
장기려는 의사로서 아픈 사람들을 무료로 도왔다.
세 사람은 모두 20세기에 생을 마쳤다.
items.exp: As a doctor, he helped sick people for free.와 일치해요. 병원을 지은 사람은 장기려이고, 마타이는 케냐에서 싸우고 아프리카에 나무를 심었으며, 마타이는 2011년에 세상을 떠났어요.
items.passage:
• Mother Teresa (1910-1997) ― She did a lot of volunteer work in Kolkata, India. She took care of sick and poor people.
• Chang Kiryo (1911-1995) ― He built a hospital to help people in need. As a doctor, he helped sick people for free.
• Wangarĩ Muta Maathai (1940-2011) ― She was a brave activist who fought for the rights of people in Kenya. She planted trees to make people's life better across Africa.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [to help]와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: I want to drink some water.
I have a lot of homework to do.
She went to the library to borrow some books.
My dream is to be a teacher.
I was glad to see you again.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 to help는 '~하기 위해서'라는 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법이에요. to borrow some books가 같아요. 나머지는 명사적, 형용사적, 명사적, 감정의 원인(부사적)이라 목적이 아니에요.
items.passage:
• Mother Teresa (1910-1997) ― She did a lot of volunteer work in Kolkata, India. She took care of sick and poor people.
• Chang Kiryo (1911-1995) ― He built a hospital [to help] people in need. As a doctor, he helped sick people for free.
• Wangarĩ Muta Maathai (1940-2011) ― She was a brave activist who fought for the rights of people in Kenya. She planted trees to make people's life better across Africa.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [who]와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: Who is that tall boy over there?
I don't know who broke the window.
Tell me who you met yesterday.
I know a girl who speaks four languages.
Who do you want to meet?
items.exp: 밑줄 친 who는 선행사 a brave activist를 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사예요. a girl who speaks ~의 who가 같고 나머지는 모두 '누구'라는 뜻의 의문사예요.
items.passage:
• Mother Teresa (1910-1997) ― She did a lot of volunteer work in Kolkata, India. She took care of sick and poor people.
• Chang Kiryo (1911-1995) ― He built a hospital to help people in need. As a doctor, he helped sick people for free.
• Wangarĩ Muta Maathai (1940-2011) ― She was a brave activist [who] fought for the rights of people in Kenya. She planted trees to make people's life better across Africa.

items.q: 윗글의 [make people's life better]와 문장 구조(5형식)가 같은 것은?
choices: The rain made the road slippery.
She made a cake for her mother.
He made me a paper hat.
My dad made breakfast this morning.
Mina made a promise to her friend.
items.exp: make people's life better는 「make + 목적어 + 형용사」의 5형식이에요. made the road slippery가 같아요. 나머지는 3형식 또는 4형식(made me a paper hat)이에요.
items.passage:
• Mother Teresa (1910-1997) ― She did a lot of volunteer work in Kolkata, India. She took care of sick and poor people.
• Chang Kiryo (1911-1995) ― He built a hospital to help people in need. As a doctor, he helped sick people for free.
• Wangarĩ Muta Maathai (1940-2011) ― She was a brave activist who fought for the rights of people in Kenya. She planted trees to [make people's life better] across Africa.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 의미 있는 활동을 찾는 학생들에게 권하는 프로젝트이다.
1월 3일에 시작해서 1월 10일에 끝난다.
동아리에 가입한 학생만 참여할 수 있다.
학생들은 지역 주민 센터에서 활동한다.
학생들이 만든 김치는 어려움에 처한 사람들에게 전해진다.
items.exp: It's a volunteer project that any student can join.과 Anyone is welcome to join!으로 보아 어떤 학생이든 참여할 수 있어요.
items.passage: Are you looking for something meaningful this winter? Then, join our school club's "The Magic of Giving" project! It's a volunteer project that any student can join. It starts on January 3 and ends on January 10. Students will work at a local community center to make kimchi and give it to people in need. Anyone is welcome to join!

items.q: 윗글의 [on January 3]의 on처럼 빈칸에 on을 쓸 수 없는 문장은?
choices: The concert is ___ Saturday evening.
My sister was born ___ March 14.
We will visit the center ___ winter.
The event starts ___ December 1.
I have a piano lesson ___ Tuesday.
items.exp: 특정한 날짜와 요일 앞에는 on을 쓰고, 계절 앞에는 in을 써요. in winter가 맞으므로 on은 쓸 수 없어요.
items.passage: Are you looking for something meaningful this winter? Then, join our school club's "The Magic of Giving" project! It's a volunteer project that any student can join. It starts [on] January 3 and ends [on] January 10. Students will work at a local community center to make kimchi and give it to people in need. Anyone is welcome to join!

items.q: 윗글을 쓴 목적으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 김치 담그는 방법을 설명하려고
지역 주민 센터를 소개하려고
프로젝트에 필요한 기부금을 요청하려고
봉사 활동 결과를 보고하려고
자원봉사 프로젝트에 참여할 학생을 모집하려고
items.exp: Then, join our school club's project!와 Anyone is welcome to join!으로 보아 참가자를 모집하는 글이에요.
items.passage: Are you looking for something meaningful this winter? Then, join our school club's "The Magic of Giving" project! It's a volunteer project that any student can join. It starts on January 3 and ends on January 10. Students will work at a local community center to make kimchi and give it to people in need. Anyone is welcome to join!

items.q: 다음 중 윗글의 [is welcome to join]과 같은 형태로 어법상 옳은 문장은?
choices: All students are welcome joining the club.
All students are welcome to joining the club.
All students are welcome to join the club.
All students are welcome join the club.
All students welcome to join the club.
items.exp: be welcome to + 동사원형은 '~하는 것을 환영받다'라는 뜻이에요. are welcome to join이 맞고 나머지는 -ing 사용, 동사원형 단독, be동사 생략으로 틀려요.
items.passage: Are you looking for something meaningful this winter? Then, join our school club's "The Magic of Giving" project! It's a volunteer project that any student can join. It starts on January 3 and ends on January 10. Students will work at a local community center to make kimchi and give it to people in need. Anyone [is welcome to join]!

items.q: 윗글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: shone은 동사를 꾸미므로 형용사 bright가 아니라 부사 brightly여야 해요. ⓑ, ⓒ는 want/decide 뒤의 to부정사, ⓓ는 전치사 for 뒤의 동명사, ⓔ는 목적격 관계대명사로 모두 맞아요.
items.passage: Summer came, and the sun shone ⓐ[bright]. It was too hot for Angus. The sparrows wanted ⓑ[to help] him, so they decided ⓒ[to make] something useful for Angus. They collected lots of leaves and made a hat for him. The hat was perfect for ⓓ[protecting] Angus from the sun, and he loved the gift ⓔ[that the sparrows made].

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [It]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: It is getting dark outside.
It is important to help others.
It is my favorite hat.
It was Angus who made the socks.
I found a sock, and it was red.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 It은 날씨·명암 등을 나타내는 비인칭 주어로 뜻이 없어요. It is getting dark가 같아요. 나머지는 가주어, 대명사, 강조 구문, 대명사예요.
items.passage: Summer came, and the sun shone brightly. [It] was too hot for Angus. The sparrows wanted to help him, so they decided to make something useful for Angus. They collected lots of leaves and made a hat for him. The hat was perfect for protecting Angus from the sun, and he loved the gift that the sparrows made.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 참새들은 겨울에 Angus에게 모자를 만들어 주었다.
Angus는 참새들이 만든 선물을 좋아하지 않았다.
참새들은 나뭇잎을 모아 Angus를 위한 모자를 만들었다.
참새들은 가게에서 산 모자를 선물했다.
모자는 Angus를 추위로부터 보호해 주었다.
items.exp: They collected lots of leaves and made a hat for him.과 일치해요. 계절은 여름이고, 모자는 햇빛으로부터 보호해 주었으며, Angus는 선물을 아주 좋아했어요.
items.passage: Summer came, and the sun shone brightly. It was too hot for Angus. The sparrows wanted to help him, so they decided to make something useful for Angus. They collected lots of leaves and made a hat for him. The hat was perfect for protecting Angus from the sun, and he loved the gift that the sparrows made.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [helped me score a goal]처럼 help 뒤의 목적격 보어가 올바르게 쓰인 문장은?
choices: Her advice helped me finding the answer.
Her advice helped my find the answer.
Her advice helped me found the answer.
Her advice helped me to finding the answer.
Her advice helped me find the answer.
items.exp: help + 목적어 + 동사원형(또는 to부정사)의 형태예요. helped me find가 맞고 finding, found, to finding은 쓸 수 없어요.
items.passage: Taeho and I became close thanks to soccer. Our team had a soccer game against another team. His pass [helped me score a goal]. After that, we became good friends.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 [against]와 의미가 같은 것은?
choices: He leaned the ladder against the wall.
The Korean team will play against Japan in the final.
I am against the new rule.
Put your back against the door.
Take this medicine against colds.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 against는 '~를 상대로, ~에 맞서'라는 뜻이에요. play against Japan이 같아요. 나머지는 '~에 기대어', '~에 반대하여', '~에 대비하여'의 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Taeho and I became close thanks to soccer. Our team had a soccer game [against] another team. His pass helped me score a goal. After that, we became good friends.

items.q: 윗글의 [thanks to]와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은? (Taeho and I became close ___ soccer.)
choices: because
instead of
in spite of
even though
because of
items.exp: thanks to는 '~ 덕분에'라는 뜻이고 뒤에 명사가 와요. 같은 자리에 명사를 취하는 because of가 의미와 문법 모두 맞아요. because와 even though는 뒤에 절이 와야 하고, instead of와 in spite of는 뜻이 달라요.
items.passage: Taeho and I became close [thanks to] soccer. Our team had a soccer game against another team. His pass helped me score a goal. After that, we became good friends.
